note.note:
Consult Summary:
- Telehealth consult for new-onset left-sided throbbing headache with photophobia for ~1 day; no red flags elicited; clinician impression likely migraine; advised NSAIDs with acetaminophen, hydration, safety-netting, BP check, and consider further evaluation if recurrent.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Severe headache for about 1 day.
- Onset/Timeline:
  - Began yesterday morning on waking.
  - Constant baseline with fluctuating intensity; never fully resolves.
  - Still present at time of consult.
- Character/Location: Throbbing, intense; mainly left-sided.
- Exacerbating/Relieving factors:
  - Worse in bright light/sunlight.
  - Feels better lying down.
  - Not worse with coughing/sneezing.
  - No clear positional worsening (lying flat or bending forward not worse).
- Associated symptoms/ROS:
  - Photophobia present.
  - Denies visual disturbance, abnormal smells/tastes, nausea, vomiting.
  - Eating and drinking normally.
  - Denies fever (has not measured temperature), skin changes/rash.
  - Denies weakness, tingling, or numbness in limbs.
  - No recent upper respiratory or ear symptoms; felt well the day before onset.
- Menstrual history: Last period ~1 week ago; headache not linked to a particular point in cycle per patient.
- Prior history of headaches: Denies prior regular headaches.
- Self-care to date: Acetaminophen (paracetamol) taken; resting at home; avoiding light.

Past Medical History:
- No significant past medical problems, hospital admissions, or surgeries reported.
- Medications:
  - Microgynon (combined oral contraceptive pill); started ~6 years ago; dose/route/frequency not documented; no notable side effects reported.
  - Acetaminophen (paracetamol) for current headache; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies:
  - Aspirin – reaction: nausea (“feel really sick”).

Social History:
- Living situation: Lives with housemates/friends.
- Tobacco: Never smoker.
- Alcohol: “A few drinks at the weekend.”
- Recreational drugs: Denies use.
- Work/stress: Possible increased work stress recently (patient unsure of trigger).

Family History:
- Mother: Hypertension; history of migraines.

Physical Examination:
- [No vitals or physical examination documented in this telehealth encounter.]

Investigations:
- None performed or documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute unilateral headache with photophobia, new onset; likely migraine without aura per clinician impression; no red flags elicited; no prior migraine history.
  - Plan:
    - Trial NSAID (e.g., ibuprofen) in combination with acetaminophen as advised.
    - Maintain good hydration.
    - Safety-net: Seek urgent care if headache worsens, changes character, persists without improvement, fever develops, new neurological symptoms occur, or rash appears.
    - If headaches become persistent, cyclical with menses, or have identifiable triggers, arrange follow-up for further evaluation and management options.
- Issue 2: Blood pressure monitoring (no recent measurement at home; historically normal).
  - Plan:
    - Arrange to have blood pressure checked (patient advised to get BP checked).
- Issue 3: Home monitoring and self-care tools.
  - Plan:
    - Obtain a home thermometer to monitor temperature during illness episodes.
- General plan items:
  - Continue to avoid aspirin due to reported adverse reaction; NSAIDs like ibuprofen/naproxen previously tolerated but not used in recent days.

Quality checks (always include at bottom of note, or fill document_quality):
- Missing expected elements:
  - No vitals obtained; no in-person neurological exam or fundoscopy.
  - No pain severity scale documented.
  - Full medication reconciliation (beyond contraceptive and acetaminophen) not documented.
  - Pregnancy status not addressed.
- Internal conflicts:
  - BP history: Patient initially stated she hasn’t had BP checked recently, then reported it was checked about 6 months ago with repeat prescription (“conflict noted”).
- Transcript quality:
  - Generally clear; minor pauses/ellipses and brief inaudible or clipped segments but clinical content understandable.
